transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SA briefly), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Halcyon), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Priya Desai (ML Eng), Ava Green (Head of Security, joined 15m in)

Optional auto-generated summary: Discussed integration options for Redwood hosted/dedicated/private. Focus on how to integrate with existing SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex, where to place gateway/proxy, rate limiting and quotas, and observability hooks. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account, and I have Ravi, our SE, with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited.
[00:10] Samir Khan: Hey \u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u2014 morning. Quick thing, we got the calendar earlier, we'll try to keep this focused on integration details.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Perfect, high level plan \u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u000B\u2014 we want to understand your use cases (real-time chat + periodic embeddings), traffic patterns, security requirements, and which deployment mode you're leaning toward (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Then Ravi will walk through integration options.
[00:30] Priya Desai: Quick intro from me \u000B\u000B\u000B\u2014 I own the ML infra and the embedding pipelines. Our main ask: low 99th percentile latency for live assist (sub-300ms ideally for internal routing) and cost control for customer-facing async tasks. We'll likely use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for doc indexing.
[00:45] Ravi Patel: Awesome. We see that pattern a lot. Redwood supports first-class SDKs plus native connectors folks use in LangChain and LlamaIndex. I'll show snippets and tradeoffs. Quick question \u000B\u000B\u2014 do you plan to run a gateway/proxy in front of Redwood or call our API directly from your services?
[01:00] Samir Khan: We prefer a centralized API gateway \u000B\u000B\u2014 helps with routing, auth, and shielding internal tokens. But we worry about client-side latency added by another hop.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Totally. Common pattern is to keep a lightweight gateway in the VPC and egress to Redwood's hosted API, or for Dedicated/Private you can keep traffic on private network paths. We'll talk through latency numbers for each.
[01:30] Priya Desai: Also curious about batching/kv caches and whether Redwood exposes hooks for LangChain to use context caching \u000B\u000B\u2014 we want to avoid re-embedding big docs.
[01:42] Ravi Patel: Yes \u000B\u000B\u2014 two things: we have automatic prefix/KV caching at the runtime level (transparent to callers) and SDK-level helpers. For LangChain/LlamaIndex you can use the SDK to persist embeddings and reuse them; we'll share examples. The runtime also supports continuous batching so throughput helps with cost.
[02:00] Lena Ortiz: Our security team will ask about SOC2, encryption at rest, and KMS. Also, for private deployments we need on-prem options.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Good point. Redwood offers Hosted with SOC2, Dedicated with customer-isolated pools, and Private for VPC or on-prem. We have a compliance pack we'll share; it covers KMS integration, audit logs, and RBAC.
[02:25] Samir Khan: Cool. How do rate limits and quotas work? We have bursty traffic \u000B\u000B\u2014 Black Friday style spikes but mostly predictable weekly spikes.
[02:34] Ravi Patel: We have per-API-key quotas, per-route limits, and tiered throttling. For Dedicated you get capacity guarantees and can configure burst capacity and autoscaling policies. For Hosted you can request rate-limit increases and we expose headers for remaining quota. We can also put a gateway in front to smooth bursts.
[02:55] Priya Desai: Is there token-level billing visibility? We need to allocate cost back to product teams.
[03:02] Maya Chen: Yes \u000B\u000B\u2014 Console has token-level cost breakdowns per route/model and per-token attribution. That integrates with billing exports.
[03:10] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection \u000B\u000B\u2014 observability hooks: we expose per-request traces, sampling, and an event stream for logs/metrics. Customers wire those into DataDog/Prometheus or our hosted dashboard.
[03:24] Ava Green: Hey, sorry I'm late. From a security perspective we want to confirm SAML SSO, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. Also interested in whether any PII leaves our VPC for hosted.
[03:36] Maya Chen: Welcome Ava. For Hosted, user data is sent to Redwood endpoints; we support encryption in transit and at rest, and you can opt for a Dedicated or Private deployment if you need strict data residency or on-prem handling. SAML and RBAC are supported; audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM.
[03:55] Lena Ortiz: Can you walk through an example LangChain flow? We're using OpenAI's SDK now \u000B\u000B\u2014 migrating would need minimal code changes.
[04:04] Ravi Patel: Sure \u000B\u000B\u2014 most folks swap the client instantiation for Redwood's SDK and keep the same LangChain connectors. Example: change OpenAI client references to RedwoodClient from our SDK, update endpoint, and the rest of the chain is the same. LlamaIndex has a connector we maintain in our docs; we'll share a snippet. There are slight differences around streaming and function-calling semantics but our SDK maps closely to the common interfaces.
[04:35] Priya Desai: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex retrieval + our embedding store? We want to run local FAISS and only send vectors to Redwood for re-ranking.
[04:44] Ravi Patel: That's supported \u000B\u000B\u2014 you can keep embeddings in your FAISS, send candidates to Redwood for reranking or generate with context. For embeddings you might prefer a batch embeddings flow to reduce cost. We'll share best practices.
[05:00] Samir Khan: About gateway/proxy placement: if we run it in our VPC, what TLS and auth patterns do you support? We intend to use mTLS internally.
[05:12] Maya Chen: You can use token-based auth or mTLS for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, token-based with a VPC egress path is common; Dedicated offers private networking, and Private can be fully on-prem with mTLS.
[05:28] Priya Desai: Latency numbers \u000B\u000B\u2014 do you have benchmarks for 128-token chat on a p4-like spec? We need P99 under 300ms for internal assist; external facing can be higher.
[05:38] Ravi Patel: We have performance profiles by model. For smaller context lengths and chatting on optimized runtimes, p99 in low hundreds is achievable on Dedicated; Hosted depends on plan and region. We'll include a benchmark spreadsheet. Note that batching and KV cache will reduce tail latency for repeated prefixes.
[06:00] Lena Ortiz: If we go Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline? We need something within 6\u20138 weeks ideally.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4\u20138 weeks depending on capacity and network config. Private on-prem can take longer \u2014 usually 8\u201312 weeks. Hosted is immediate and good for early validation.
[06:20] Samir Khan: For quotas, can we have per-team limits and alerting when teams near spend thresholds?
[06:28] Ravi Patel: Yes \u2014 we have per-route and per-team quotas, alerting integrations, and can export usage to your billing system for chargeback. You can set quotas in the console and programmatically via API.
[06:42] Priya Desai: Observability \u2014 do we get traces that show model latency per-token and breakdowns across tokenization/forward pass/IO?
[06:50] Jordan Lee: We provide per-token breakdowns where instrumentation allows, plus traces that annotate kernel time vs IO. It's not always down to every kernel, but we show the important buckets that affect latency and cost.
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: On compliance \u2014 if we go Hosted, is there an option to restrict model logging or opt out of retention?
[07:13] Maya Chen: Yes \u2014 retention policies are configurable; you can opt out of storing request/response payloads for Hosted, or choose shorter retention. For strict requirements Private/Dedicated is recommended so you control logs entirely.
[07:27] Samir Khan: Let's talk about error handling and fallbacks. If a model is overloaded, can requests default to a smaller model automatically?
[07:35] Ravi Patel: Yes \u2014 Redwood routing policies support automatic fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost tiers. You can define policy by latency, cost, or region.
[07:46] Priya Desai: Will LangChain chains that depend on function-calling still behave the same? There are subtle differences in streaming tokens and function call wrappers.
[07:55] Ravi Patel: We support tool/function calling and streaming; our SDK's method signatures mirror common libs. There are small integration notes we'll capture in the snippet.
[08:10] Lena Ortiz: Any limits on model versions? We want to pin to a specific model for consistency in production.
[08:17] Maya Chen: You can pin model versions in the deployment config and use rollout policies for canary or A/B. The Console shows model versioning and per-version metrics.
[08:30] Samir Khan: For the POC, we'd like to test a LangChain-based chat flow with 100 QPS sustained and 500 QPS bursts, embeddings for nightly indexing, and reranking. Can you support benchmarking?
[08:42] Ravi Patel: Absolutely \u2014 we'll provide a benchmark harness and suggested test plan. For Hosted we'll advise on rate limits; for Dedicated we'll size GPU pools to meet throughput targets.
[08:55] Priya Desai: On the embeddings side, we also want a sample LlamaIndex connector that preserves metadata and allows rerank calls.
[09:02] Ravi Patel: We'll share an example and a repo link.
[09:07] Ava Green: Security question \u2014 do you support customer-managed KMS keys for encrypted at-rest storage?
[09:14] Maya Chen: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; for Hosted we have managed encryption but can discuss key access models in the security pack.
[09:28] Lena Ortiz: How do we handle regional restrictions? Some EU customers require data residency in EU.
[09:35] Maya Chen: We have regional endpoints and can deploy Dedicated capacity in EU regions. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated deployed in a region that meets the requirement.
[09:50] Jordan Lee: Quick note about SDKs \u2014 we provide first-class SDKs in Python/TS/Go and a LangChain-specific helper package. LlamaIndex connectors are in our docs and a maintained gist.
[09:59] Samir Khan: Any concerns about vendor lock-in when using Redwood SDKs with LangChain?
[10:05] Ravi Patel: We try to keep interfaces compatible; most customers keep the orchestration in LangChain and swap clients, so lock-in is low. You can always keep a thin adapter layer in your codebase.
[10:20] Priya Desai: For the POC we'll need sample configs for rate limiting and autoscale. Can you share recommended autoscaling policies for spikes?
[10:28] Ravi Patel: Yes \u2014 we'll include policy templates; for Dedicated you can set target latency SLOs and autoscale GPU pools accordingly, with burst buffers for short spikes.
[10:40] Lena Ortiz: Who will be our primary SE during the POC?
[10:45] Maya Chen: Ravi will lead SE support; Jordan will be on-call for infra-level questions.
[10:50] Samir Khan: Are there any network requirements (firewall rules, IP allowlist) for calling Redwood Hosted endpoints?
[10:57] Maya Chen: We publish egress IP ranges for Hosted and we also support PrivateLink in some regions; Dedicated gives you a customer-dedicated endpoint.
[11:08] Priya Desai: For tracing integration, do you expose OpenTelemetry spans natively?
[11:14] Jordan Lee: We emit spans compatible with OTLP and provide SDK hooks for automatic span injection. You can correlate with your service traces.
[11:25] Ava Green: On incident response \u2014 do you provide runbooks or playbooks for when models degrade or throughput drops?
[11:32] Maya Chen: Yes \u2014 we have runbooks for common incidents, escalation contacts, and a playbook for automatic failover to fallback models. That's in the enterprise support pack.
[11:45] Lena Ortiz: Cost: can you provide a model for expected tokens per 1M messages and what that translates to spend for hosted vs dedicated buckets? We need to compare unit economics.
[11:54] Ravi Patel: We'll prepare a cost model: token usage \u00d7 model cost per token, plus compute allocation for Dedicated. We'll show break-even points for Dedicated vs Hosted by monthly token volume.
[12:10] Samir Khan: Any limitations with streaming responses and function calls when going through our gateway?
[12:18] Ravi Patel: Streaming should work fine through a proxy if you support chunked transfer and don't buffer end-to-end. Function calls will serialize similarly; avoid proxies that fully buffer.
[12:32] Priya Desai: Are there SDKs or helpers for retries with idempotency in case of network errors?
[12:38] Jordan Lee: Yes \u2014 client SDK has built-in retry/backoff with idempotency keys support and guidance for when to use them.
[12:50] Lena Ortiz: OK, sounds good. Let's prioritize the next steps: pricing, security docs, LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, and a POC scoping call.
[12:59] Maya Chen: Great. We'll send the security pack and pricing by tomorrow, Ravi will push code samples this week, and we'll aim to set the scoping call for Sep 21.
[13:10] Samir Khan: Quick alignment \u2014 for the POC we expect to run a smoke test on Hosted first and then move to Dedicated if performance and cost line up.
[13:20] Maya Chen: That's a common approach \u2014 Hosted to validate, Dedicated to commit once we see steady traffic.
[13:30] Priya Desai: One last thing \u2014 can you include a short checklist of what we should provide to size Dedicated (token profile, QPS, retention)?
[13:38] Ravi Patel: We'll include a sizing checklist: RPS/QPS, average tokens per request, concurrency, burst profile, latency SLOs, model choices, and retention/usage patterns.
[13:50] Ava Green: We'll also list compliance point people and required SLAs.
[13:55] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc pack.
[14:00] Lena Ortiz: Appreciate it. Talk soon.

End transcript.

References mentioned: pricing spreadsheet (link to be shared), security pack (SOC2/KMS docs), LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo (link to be shared), benchmarking harness (internal Redwood link).
